name: Rosewood Miyakojima
positioning: Beachfront resort of villas and houses on Miyakojima in Okinawa, inspired by modern Japanese minimalism and the culture of the Ryukyu Islands
best_for: Families or groups wanting a two-bedroom villa with a private pool and BBQ area
Travelers who want water sports from the beach, spa time and local craft experiences

facts.text: Rosewood Miyakojima is set at Nikadori in the Hirara area of Miyakojima.
The resort buildings trace the curve of the shoreline.
The resort is inspired by modern Japanese minimalism and shaped by the culture of the Ryukyu Islands.
The Beachfront Villa opens directly onto the sand and the ocean.
UPRA House is a two-bedroom villa with a private pool and indoor and outdoor dining, including a BBQ area.
Nagi, named for the calm of the sea, serves Italian cuisine.
Choma offers four expressions of Japanese cuisine beside the sea.
Asaya Spa rituals are rooted in the island's herbs and oils and the five elements.
Guests can step from the beach in front of the resort to go stand-up paddleboarding, kayaking and snorkeling.
Guests can unwind in a private cabana by the sea.

highlights.text: KAMII House is a two-bedroom villa on the tip of the resort's peninsula.
Choma Bar is a quiet bar whose cocktails are inspired by the stories of Miyako's eight islands.
Guests can join the resort's efforts to protect Miyakojima's native horses, of which fewer than 50 remain.
Guests can try adan weaving, a local craft that uses the native Adan tree.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes that the remote island location requires flight connections.
WhataHotel notes ultra-premium pricing that reflects the resort's luxury positioning.
